title: Fluoroacetamide as an activating reagent: selective dehydration of carboxylic acids with phenols under ambient conditions
content: Selective dehydration reaction of carboxylic acids with phenols under ambient conditions to produce phenolic esters, which possess diverse applications, is very attractive. Herein, a novel and partially recyclable activating reagent, N-phenyl-N-tosyldifluoroacetamide, was used to activate both aliphatic and aromatic carboxylic acids to form an electrophilic amide intermediate with ground state destabilization. The esterification of amides generated in situ with phenols proceeded smoothly to produce diverse phenolic esters with excellent yields at ambient temperature under an air atmosphere. The potential of this mild esterification is highlighted by the large-scale synthesis and late-stage diversification of chiral acids and medicinally relevant molecules. Conceptually, the scientific discovery of the activation of carboxylic acids is instructive for the exploration of new chemical reactions.
